en: Stretched into long lanes and streets
One household grills meat, ten thousand households smell the fragrance
Temple, the sound of the wooden fish
Knock, knock, knocking out a path
Fish that forget each other in the rivers and lakes

points.zh:
「 泉涸，魚相與處於陸，相呴以溼，相濡以沫，不如相忘於江湖。」
--莊子《 內篇:  大宗師 》
points.en:
"When the springs dry up and the fish are left stranded together on the land, they moisten each other with their damp breath and wet each other with their spittle—better that they should forget one another in the rivers and lakes."
--Zhuangzi, "Inner Chapters: The Great and Venerable Teacher"

points.zh: 米勒 ( Jean-Francois Millt,1814-1875)，法國巴比松派畫家，以鄉村風俗寫實，描繪農村生活而聞名，是法國最偉大的田園畫家。羅曼·羅蘭在所著的《米勒傳》指出：「米勒，這位將全部精神灌注於永恆的意義勝過剎那的古典大師，從來就沒有一位畫家像他這般，將萬物所歸的大地給予如此雄壯又偉大的感覺與表現。」著名畫作《晚鐘》( 又名《晚禱 》)，描繪兩位務農夫婦聽到向晚的鐘聲，虔誠低頭禱告的情景。遠處有教堂尖塔，聳立在黃昏的田野上，兩人的剪影凸顯於斜陽餘暉的背景中。《晚鐘》雖然以描繪自然景色為出發點，但是二位人物的姿勢，在畫家筆下，彷彿在頌揚大自然給予人類的恩賜，以及人類謙恭柔順的感恩。米勒以親切的畫風語言，真實地反映農民的難苦勤勞和自足感恩的日常生活。此畫是巴黎奧塞美術舘的典藏之寶。其他的代表畫作有 : 《拾穗》，《播種者》和《牧羊少女》等。
points.en: Millet (Jean-Francois Millet, 1814–1875), painter of the French Barbizon School, renowned for his realistic depictions of rural customs and peasant life, is considered France's greatest painter of rural life. Romain Rolland, in his biography of Millet, wrote: "Millet, this classical master who poured his whole spirit into the eternal rather than the fleeting moment, was unlike any other painter in the grand and magnificent feeling and expression he gave to the earth to which all things return." His famous painting 'The Angelus' (also called 'Evening Prayer') depicts two farming spouses who, upon hearing the evening bell, bow their heads in devout prayer. In the distance, a church spire rises over the fields at dusk, the two figures' silhouettes set against the backdrop of the fading evening light. Although 'The Angelus' begins from a depiction of natural scenery, the postures of the two figures, under the painter's brush, seem to celebrate the blessings nature bestows upon humankind and the humble, grateful submission of human beings. Millet, in an intimate pictorial language, faithfully reflects the hard toil and self-sufficient gratitude of peasant daily life. This painting is a treasured holding of the Musee d'Orsay in Paris. His other representative works include 'The Gleaners,' 'The Sower,' and 'The Shepherdess.'

en: The years drift, and still I remember
The setting sun where the grass's color ends

points.zh:
A.  貝聿銘作品: 法國巴黎羅浮宮玻璃金字塔 (1989年)。 今年 ( 2019 ) 慶祝落成30年。這是貝聿銘建築作品中最為人讚嘆，津津樂道的建築，是巴黎的地標，法國的驕傲，建築之光，是融合現代與古典的建築範例。是一顆自天外飛來的璀燦寶石。貝聿銘認為，玻璃金字塔提供了 一個擁有歷史價值和比喻意義的象徵性入口，寓意連接現代與古代。
B.  貝聿銘作品: 中國江蘇蘇州博物館 ( 2006 )。 這是貝聿銘最鍾愛女兒般，掌上明珠的作品。延續蘇州傳統建築，巧妙的借助水面與相鄰的拙政園相互呼應，以水墨畫的飄逸和清盈，散文性的抒情意境，把創新與傳統結合，造就恰到好處之江南園林新格局。號稱是貝聿銘「封刀之作」。
C.  貝聿銘 (I. M. Pei，1917 ~ 2019) 華裔美籍，一代建築大師，逝世於2019年5月16日，享年102歲。貝聿銘生於蘇州傳奇家族，卻用百年時間，締造了屬於他自己的傳奇人生。有“中國最後的貴族 ”，“現代建築的最後大師” 之稱謂。他把畢生的聰明才智，融進一棟棟現代化的建築設計之中，聳立在全世界四大洲的10個國家。「讓光來作設計」是他的名言。他曾說：「名譽如浮雲，生不帶來死不帶去。真正能留在人世間的，就只有建築。」而他留給世人最好的建築，或許是樹築於時間之上的那顆赤子之心，永遠跳躍的遠望吧!
貝聿銘小檔案
1917年 4 月26日出生於中國廣州
學歷:   麻省理工學建築學士，哈佛大學建築碩士
華裔美籍建築師, 被譽稱「現代主義建築最後大師」
1981年美國國家藝術委員會「榮譽金獎」（Gold Medal of Honor）
1983年榮獲有建築界諾貝爾獎美譽的普利兹克獎 ( Pritzker Architecture Prize )
1992年獲美國總統布希授與美國總統自由勳章
2009年英國皇家建築師學會皇家金獎 （Royal Gold Medal )
代表建築作品 :   台灣東海大學路思義教堂 (1963) ，美國纽约州康乃爾大學約翰遜藝術館 (1973 ) ，美國華盛頓特區國家美術館東館 (1978) ，巴黎羅浮宮金字塔 (1989) ，香港中國銀行大厦 (1990) ，日本滋賀縣甲賀市美秀美術館 (1997) ，美國克利夫蘭搖滾音樂名堂 (1998) ，台灣新北市八里垃圾焚化廠 (2001) ，中國江蘇省蘇州博物舘 (2006) ，卡達杜哈伊斯蘭藝術博物館 (2008 )。
points.en:
A. I. M. Pei's work: the Louvre Pyramid in Paris, France (1989). This year (2019) marks the 30th anniversary of its completion. Among I. M. Pei's architectural works, this is the one most admired and most often discussed -- a landmark of Paris, a source of pride for France, a beacon of architecture, and an exemplar of blending the modern with the classical. It is like a brilliant gem fallen from the sky. Pei believed the glass pyramid offered a symbolic entrance imbued with historical value and metaphorical meaning, signifying a connection between the modern and the ancient.
B. I. M. Pei's work: the Suzhou Museum in Jiangsu, China (2006). This is the work Pei cherished most, like a beloved daughter, the apple of his eye. Continuing Suzhou's traditional architectural style, it skillfully uses water surfaces to echo the adjacent Humble Administrator's Garden, combining innovation with tradition through the flowing lightness of ink-wash painting and a prose-like lyrical mood, achieving a new form of Jiangnan garden design that strikes just the right balance. It is often called Pei's "final masterpiece."
C. I. M. Pei (1917-2019), a Chinese-American architect and a master of his generation, passed away on May 16, 2019, at the age of 102. Born into a legendary family in Suzhou, Pei spent a century forging a legend all his own. He has been called "China's last aristocrat" and "the last master of modern architecture." He poured a lifetime of brilliance into one modern architectural design after another, works that now stand in 10 countries across four continents. "Let the light do the design" was one of his famous sayings. He once said: "Fame is like floating clouds -- it comes with neither birth nor death. What truly remains in this world is only architecture." And perhaps the finest structure he left behind is the innocent heart he built above and beyond time -- a heart that will forever leap and gaze into the distance.
I. M. Pei, brief profile
Born April 26, 1917, in Guangzhou, China
Education: Bachelor of Architecture from MIT, Master of Architecture from Harvard University
Chinese-American architect, celebrated as "the last master of modernist architecture"
1981: Gold Medal of Honor from the American National Arts Club
1983: Awarded the Pritzker Architecture Prize, often called the Nobel Prize of architecture
1992: Awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom by U.S. President George H. W. Bush
2009: Royal Gold Medal from the Royal Institute of British Architects
Representative works: Luce Memorial Chapel at Tunghai University, Taiwan (1963); Johnson Museum of Art at Cornell University, New York, USA (1973); East Building of the National Gallery of Art, Washington, D.C., USA (1978); the Louvre Pyramid, Paris (1989); Bank of China Tower, Hong Kong (1990); Miho Museum, Koka, Shiga Prefecture, Japan (1997); Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, Cleveland, USA (1998); Bali Waste Incineration Plant, New Taipei City, Taiwan (2001); Suzhou Museum, Jiangsu, China (2006); Museum of Islamic Art, Doha, Qatar (2008).

points.zh:
**
《最後的住家》 (台語)
詩: 馬偕   曲: 鄭智仁，李奎然
我全心所疼惜的台灣啊！  我的青春攏總獻給你，
我專心所疼惜的台灣啊！  我一生的歡喜攏在此。
我在雲霧中看見山嶺，  從雲中隙孔觀望全地，
波浪大海中遙遠的對岸，  我意愛在此晀望無息。
我心未通割離的台灣啊！  我的人生攏總獻給你，
我心未通割離的台灣啊！  我一世的快樂攏在此。
盼望我人生中的續尾站，  在大湧拍岸的響聲中，
在竹林搖動陰影的裡面，  找著我一生最後住家。
朱真一醫師:  「馬偕〈最後的住家〉詩: 兩日文版的意義及關聯」( 台北市醫師公會會刊， 2019年第63卷第3期 83~87 頁 )
朱真一醫師: 「馬偕的〈最後的住家〉的故事」( 民報 2014-06-22 )
points.en:
**
「My Last Home」 (in Taiwanese)
Poem: George Leslie Mackay  Music: Cheng Chih-jen, Li Kuei-jan
Oh Taiwan, whom I love with all my heart! I have devoted all my youth to you,
Oh Taiwan, whom I love with all my heart! All the joy of my life lies here.
Amid the clouds and mist I see the mountain ridges, through gaps in the clouds I look out over the whole land,
Across the rolling waves toward the distant far shore, I am content to gaze here without rest.
Oh Taiwan, from whom my heart cannot bear to part! I have devoted my whole life to you,
Oh Taiwan, from whom my heart cannot bear to part! All the happiness of my life lies here.
I hope that at the last stop of my life, amid the sound of great waves breaking on the shore,
Within the swaying shadows of the bamboo grove, I will find the last home of my life.
Dr. Chu Chen-yi: "Mackay's Poem 'My Last Home': The Significance of and Connections Between the Two Japanese-Language Versions" (Journal of the Taipei Physicians' Association, 2019, vol. 63, no. 3, pp. 83-87).
Dr. Chu Chen-yi: "The Story of Mackay's 'My Last Home'" (The People's News (Min Pao), June 22, 2014).

points.zh:
馬偕（Rev. George Leslie MacKay，1844年3月21日〜1901年6月2日，又稱偕叡理）因其宣教上之成就獲贈神學博士，而稱馬偕博士，台灣俗眾以「黑鬚番」外號稱他；加拿大首位海外宣教師。1872年三月上陸滬尾（今淡水），擇此地進行在台傳道、醫療和教育的基地。近30年間不只宣揚基督教義，建立北台灣基督長老教會，他所建立的醫院和學校，也成為台灣現代化的里程碑，對啟迪民智、開通思想和轉化社會風氣，均有深遠之貢獻。他以淡水為家，在此娶妻生子，融入庶民生活，死後埋骨淡水砲台埔。一生傳奇為這北台灣帶來豐富的文化風情，他對台灣的愛與認同，更可啟發今日的台灣住民。
(  摘自台灣敎會公報 )
林衡哲醫師:「 認同台灣熱愛台灣宣教士馬偕 (1844~1901) 」( 民報2016-06-12 )
points.en:
George Leslie MacKay (March 21, 1844 – June 2, 1901), also known by his Chinese name Kai Jai-Li, is commonly called Dr. MacKay in recognition of his achievements in missionary work, for which he received an honorary doctorate in theology; ordinary Taiwanese nicknamed him the 'Black-Bearded Barbarian.' He was Canada's first overseas missionary. In March 1872 he landed at Hobe (present-day Tamsui), choosing this location as his base for missionary, medical, and educational work in Taiwan. Over nearly thirty years, he not only spread the Christian faith and established the Presbyterian Church in northern Taiwan, but the hospitals and schools he founded also became milestones in Taiwan's modernization, making a profound contribution to enlightening the public, opening up new ways of thinking, and transforming social customs. He made Tamsui his home, married and raised children there, and lived among ordinary people; after his death he was buried at Hobe Fort in Tamsui. His remarkable life brought rich cultural experience to northern Taiwan, and his love for and identification with Taiwan continues to inspire the people of Taiwan today.
(Excerpted from the Taiwan Church News)
Dr. Lin Heng-che: "Recognizing Taiwan, Loving Taiwan: Missionary George Leslie MacKay (1844–1901)" (Taiwan People News, June 12, 2016)
